title: The grouping algebra — collapse to region, and its exact inverse
summary: Zach's bread-and-butter operation, as pure functions over BlockScene: classify what crosses a boundary, promote the crossers to ports on a new Region node, and dissolve it again. The round trip is exact — collapse then dissolve returns a scene deep-equal to the input, array order and edge ids included.
intro: Zach's framing. "This is going to be the bread and butter of what we are doing here!!!" — and "A lot of design is basically just changing how we are grouping and ungrouping things."

The headline finding is a negative one, and it shrinks the job. Zach asked for "this line intersection logic with the port edge... we should implement pure functions for it as it's used again and again — kind of it should take a trace in, and output like a location out". That function already exists in this repo. src/components/elbow/boundaryCrossing.ts is a byte-for-byte SystemSketch copy of a Liang–Barsky clipper whose own docstring already names this exact use case, verbatim: "a group or frame boundary port, for a cable that crosses in or out of a collapsed group". So no second clipper was written. scene/portEdgeCrossing.ts is a thin adapter that adds the one number the donor does not compute — position along the wall, rather than along the polyline segment that happened to straddle it.
Everything below is a pure function. No React, no DOM, no canvas engine, and src/components/** and src/hosts/** are untouched — the rendering lane's write set was never entered.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/portEdgeCrossing.ts — new: "trace in, location out". An ADAPTER over components/elbow/boundaryCrossing.ts (not a second clipper), adding `alongSide` (0..1 along the wall, in the rail's own reading direction), route-vs-chord provenance for Bezier routes that have no vertices, and inset-consistent normalisation.

apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/region.ts — new: Region as a SceneNode `type` (Zach: "100% its a node"), plus descendantsOf / selectionRoots / absolutePosition / ancestorsOf / boundsOfNodes. Every walk is cycle-safe against a malformed parentId.

apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/boundary.ts — new: classifyBoundary (Zach's show/hide sentence, one class per clause) and promoteBoundary with a named, swappable PromotionPolicy — dagPolarityPolicy (his v1, the default) and crossingGeometryPolicy (the falsifier).
apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/collapse.ts — new: collapseToRegion and dissolveRegion (exported also as deleteNodeRewiring — one implementation, two names).
apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/boundaryWiring.ts — new: the wire helpers. Auto-port defaults to OFF, which is the feature: "having it off is nice cause then you think in terms of public api first."
apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/Grouping.stories.tsx — new: 4 stories, story-local markup only, zero component imports.
docs/GROUPING-ALGEBRA.md — new: the one argument that does not fit in a file header (§1, the view-projection vs document-mutation fork).
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — appended the five-file table, including an explicit note on what was NOT read and therefore not cited.
findings: BASELINE measured before writing anything, not trusted from the brief: tsc clean, 40 unit files / 744 tests, 62 story files / 268 stories. AFTER: tsc clean, 45 unit files / 844 tests (+5 files, +100 tests), 63 story files / 272 stories (+1 file, +4 stories). Every pre-existing test still passes; nothing was edited outside the new files plus the two docs.

THE ROUND TRIP IS EXACT, and asserted as scene equality rather than set equality: collapse then dissolve returns a scene deep-equal to the input — every edge id, both ends, both handles, `data`, and ARRAY INDEX; every node id, type, data, definitionId and array index. That is only possible because a collapse re-points the existing edge in place (keeping its id, data and index) and appends a stub, so dissolve restores the original record rather than an equivalent new one.

THE ONE LOSSY CASE, found by search rather than assumed: node positions with FRACTIONAL coordinates drift by at most one relative ulp, because re-parenting rebases by `local − origin` and dissolve restores by `local + origin`, and `(a − r) + r` is not always `a` in IEEE-754. A 3.3M-pair search (random over 12 orders of magnitude, plus adversarial decimal grids) found 16% of values inexact, worst absolute error 5.8e-11 at magnitude 3.7e5. Integer coordinates — the normal case — are exact. It does not compound past the first round trip. The first draft of this test asserted the error was below Number.EPSILON and FAILED at exactly Number.EPSILON: that bound is the gap between doubles near 1.0, so the correct bound is relative, not absolute. Corrected rather than loosened.

WHERE ZACH'S v1 FIRST BREAKS: a FEEDBACK EDGE. v1 reads polarity and calls a source "right"; under a DAG that is also downstream, so right is where the cable goes. On a feedback edge the consumer sits upstream — to the LEFT on the canvas — so the polarity stays correct and the SIDE is wrong. This is reachable in a scene the judge will happily commit: DEFAULT_CONNECTION_POLICY.allowCycles is true and findCycles treats a cycle as "the linter's real input". crossingGeometryPolicy gets it right by measuring the wall the cable actually meets, and the disagreement is an assertion, not a caption.

TWO PREDICTED BREAKS THAT DO NOT REPRODUCE. A parallel lane reading maxGraph predicted v1 "first fails when BOTH ends of an edge are folded, or when folds NEST". Both were built as tests and BOTH LAND CORRECTLY under this scene contract — because each container is classified independently, and the endpoint rewrite preserves orientation, so the second fold's DAG assumption is still reading a true fact. What DOES degrade at a second fold is the PROVENANCE, not the answer: the far end is now a promoted port id the caller's directionOf cannot resolve, so the verdict drops from by:"polarity" to by:"gesture". Composing promotedDirectionOf(regionId, ports) restores the reading — same answer, honest provenance. That composition is a passing test, not a suggestion.

A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, flagged rather than bent to fit. The same lane argued promotion should be a render-time projection that never edits the document (maxGraph's GraphView.ts:1656-1679). We kept that stance for the QUERY — classifyBoundary and promoteBoundary are pure derivations that mutate nothing, so "preview this fold without committing" is already available — and rejected it for the OPERATION, because three of Zach's rulings are unsatisfiable by a projection: a collapse MINTS a node ("100% its a node"), isolation must be structural rather than remembered ("100% region is isolated"), and a cable must survive its child being deleted ("the cables can remain wired if they go through the ports on the parent edge"), which it can only do by naming the PORT. Note the same lane's own second point — that a container's port list is a MANIFEST, not a live view over children — is incompatible with the projection reading and implied by ours. This is the lane's one decision-record candidate; per docs/peps/README.md it lands at merge, not before.

MUTATION-TESTED, three load-bearing rules, each reverted and restored: (1) normalising `t` against the un-inset box instead of the inset one — the inset test goes red with `expected +0 to be close to 0.0417`; (2) dropping the position rebase in collapse — SEVEN tests go red, the whole round-trip family; (3) inverting Zach's v1 `outerIsSink ? "right" : "left"` — FIVE tests go red. All three restored and byte-diffed clean against their backups; 844/844 green afterwards.

THE INTERSECTION PRIMITIVE IS CHECKED AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE, not against the clipper's own formula: the crossing point on a diagonal segment is verified by similar triangles, `y = y0 + (X−x0)(y1−y0)/(x1−x0)`, which is a different derivation path from the parametric Liang–Barsky under test. Asserting the clipper's own algebra back at it would be the implementation grading its own homework.

OWED TO THE RENDERING LANE, and the only thing it must add: `seat: "header"` names the RIGHT-wall twin of blockPort.layout.ts:456's functionPortCenterPx, which today computes only the LEFT one. The missing closed form is `{x: bands.blockLeft + bands.blockWidth, y: (bands.headerTop + bands.bodyTop) / 2}`. We state the seat; we do not paint it. Separately: a lane landed `collapsedWallCenterPx(bands, edge)` elsewhere and it is NOT PRESENT in this worktree, so its signature could not be matched — but the layers differ anyway (ours is {side, t} in SCENE space; src/scene/ has no bands and no px), so the natural seam is ours feeding theirs rather than one matching the other.

COMPOSED RATHER THAN REWRITTEN: lint.ts's PortDirectionOf/PortTypeOf/TypeCompatible resolvers and its source/sink vocabulary (this module refuses to be the third spelling alongside port.layout.ts's input/output); edgeValidation.ts's ConnectionOrientation.by words and its CROSS_SCOPE refusal code; linking.ts's DeletedNodeEdgePolicy ("drop"/"dangle"/"park") verbatim for the unbacked-port remainder; batchWire.ts's sharedParentId reading; sceneWires.ts's portId:"" spelling for a handle-less end; and scene.ts's findDanglingEdges injected-resolver shape for BoxOf. scene.ts itself was NOT edited.

ONE UNRESOLVED OBSERVATION, not dismissed: the story-building agent saw a single DIVERGED on the RoundTrip story from one narrowly-scoped vitest invocation immediately after writing the file. I re-ran that exact command 5/5 clean and read the fixture for shared mutable state — `fixture()` returns a fresh object per call and the only story that mutates it pushes onto its own copy — so there is no shared-fixture bug and the round-trip math is deterministic. Consistent with a cold-transform race; reported because it was seen, not because it reproduced.

sections.heading: The split edge — why the inverse is derivable instead of remembered
sections.html:
A collapse could have remembered what each container port stood for, in a data.promotedPorts side-table on the region node. That was the obvious design and it is the wrong one: the scene would carry a fact only this module could maintain, it would go stale the moment anything else edited the region, and findDanglingEdges could never check it.

Instead a collapse splits each crossing edge in two and leaves both halves in the scene — which is what a hierarchical netlist has always done, a hierarchical pin with a net on each side:

before   outerNode/o ──────────────────────────────► innerNode/i

after    outerNode/o ──► region/p          region/p ──► innerNode/i
          (the SAME edge — id, data and     (a new STUB edge, minted id,
           array index all preserved,        removed again on dissolve)
           only the inner end re-pointed)

Three things fall out for free. The region is genuinely isolated — nothing outside names anything inside any more, which is Zach's ruling as a structural property rather than a rule someone must obey. Dissolve is derivable — splicing outer → region/p with region/p → inner is exactly his "unwire helper". And the outer half keeps its identity, which is what lets the round trip be asserted as scene equality rather than set equality.

sections.heading: The data shape the rendering lane consumes
sections.html:
One PromotedPort per inside endpoint, not one per crossing edge — two outside members reading the same inner output is one thing leaving the container, drawn once and fanned.

FieldMeaning
idPort id on the container. Caller-minted; default portKey(inner.nodeId, inner.portId). Never a display name — litegraph keys its rows by name and renaming silently orphans every reference; this repo's portKey rule already forbids it.
sideBlockSide. Already resolved, so a host need not run portSideForDirection itself.
direction"source" | "sink" — lint.ts's vocabulary, not port.layout.ts's "input" | "output". Two spellings already exist in this repo; the scene layer speaks the one PortDirectionOf returns. Map at the view boundary: source → output → right.
seat"header" — the header band's centre line, Zach's chosen mechanism. "rail" — an ordinary PortEdge slot.
bandRailBand; "block" for a promoted port — the band that spans the header. "body" cannot reach header height (blockPort.layout.ts:155).
t0..1 along the wall, in the wall's reading direction. Present only when a policy actually measured it. Absent means "the rail distributes it" — not a number to invent here.
inner / outerThe endpoint inside, and every endpoint outside now reaching through this port.
edgeIdsThe edges that collapsed into it, scene order.
portTypeThe inner endpoint's declared type when typeOf states one, narrowed to one string (arePortTypesCompatible compares one to one). The narrowing is stated, not silent.
by"polarity" (a real direction was read) / "gesture" (the DAG assumption did the work) / "geometry" (measured off the cable).

And the intersection primitive's signature, which the rendering lane asked for:

portEdgeLocation(
  geometry: readonly ElbowPoint[] | { start: ElbowPoint; end: ElbowPoint },
  box: ElbowRect,
  options?: { direction?: "exit" | "enter"; inset?: number; epsilon?: number },
): { side: BlockSide; t: number; point: ElbowPoint;
     direction: "exit" | "enter"; distance: number;
     by: "route" | "chord" } | null

Plus portEdgeCrossings (all crossings, path order), portEdgeLocationPerBox (a port per nesting level in one pass), alongSide (the remap alone), and tracePolyline(route, chord) which turns a TraceRoute — whose points is null for a Bezier, by that type's own deliberate contract — into a polyline plus an honest by.

stories.title: Round trip — collapse, then dissolve, returns the identical scene
stories.look_for: Three columns: Before, Collapsed, Dissolved. In the middle column the two crossing edges have been re-pointed at the region's ports and two stubs appended; in the right column everything is back, including ids and array order. The verdict reads IDENTICAL.

stories.title: Boundary classification — Zach's rule, one class per clause
stories.look_for: One row per edge. Exactly one inbound, one outbound, two interior (hidden), one exterior — the three classes his sentence names plus the one it does not mention because it is not a candidate.

stories.title: Promoted ports — the data the rendering lane paints
stories.look_for: A sink on the left wall, a source on the right — Zach's v1 heuristic resolved. The table beside it is every field of the PromotedPort contract, including the `by` provenance.

stories.title: Where v1 first breaks — the feedback edge
stories.look_for: Two answers side by side for the same cable: v1 says side `right`, the geometry policy says `left`, and BOTH say direction `source`. Polarity right, side wrong — which is exactly what "assumes functional DAG" gives away.
